To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TCR ligation causes recruitment and activation of WASP to sites of T cell activation, and that the adaptor protein, CrkL, is a key player in this process.
the ZAP70-CrkL pathway and PKC theta link the TCR to WASF1 activation.

1) TCR-induced phosphorylation of Wasp inhibitor protein (WIP) releases WIP from the WASP-WIP complex, 2) WIP is phosphorylated by PKCtheta, and 3) WIP is recruited to the T cell receptor complex via the adaptor proteins ZAP-70 and CrkL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of recruitment of WASPs to the immunological and the activation of WASP following TCR lignment.
the molecular mechanisms of actin polymerization in T lymphocytes, and how this is linked to TCR activation.
the mechanisms of T cell activation and the role of WASP in these mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TCR engagement leads to the recruitment of CrkL, ZAP-70, WIP and WASP to the TCR microcluster, where CrkL and ZAP-70 are phosphorylated.
TCR ligation causes the formation of a complex containing ZAP-70, CrkL, WIP, WASP, and PKCtheta.
TCR engagement results in the formation and activation of a ZAP70-CrkL-PKCtheta-WIP-WASP-actin complex, which is critical for the polymerization of F-actin and T cell activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TCR ligation leads to the activation of ZAP-70 and the recruitment of the adaptor protein Crkl to the plasma membrane through binding of the SH3 domains of Crkl to phosphotyrosine residues on the ZAP- 70 molecule.
WASP activation is a multi-step process, which requires the sequential recruitment and activation of WASP by the TCR.
the TCR signal to F-actin assembly is mediated by a ZAP- 70-CrkL-PKCtheta-WIP-WASP cascade, and that the TCR-CD28 signal is mediated through a ZAP-90-PLCgamma1-CrkL-PLCgamma2-WIP-WASP pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WIP, which is a known inhibitor of WASP, can also serve to link the TCR to WAS.
the ZAP70-CrkL complex is required for TCR-induced activation of WASP.
TCR engagement causes the formation of the ZAP-7o-CrkL-WASP complex, and that the ZAP70-CrkL interaction is important for T cell activation, and that WIP is an important regulator of WASP activation.
